meta.name: NY-Style Pizza Dough
meta.description: Classic NY-style pizza dough with a 30-minute autolyse and stand mixer knead. A 62% hydration dough that stretches thin with a puffy, foldable crust.

change_log.summary: Feedback session: added agent tips on sugar reduction at high temps (ADD_ENRICHMENTS) and parm flavor bridge layering (TOP_PIZZA).
Added bake photos, fixed mozzarella notes (HEB whole milk, not TJ's), added ingredient note on mozz spec.
Scaled dough and toppings ×1.25 for bigger pizzas (~388g balls). 2 pizzas, more dough per pie.
Initial recipe from Jacob Burton / Stella Culinary

actual_yield.notes: Smaller pizzas, ~4 slices each — roughly half normal yield

cook_log.summary: First pizza bake — 1-day cold proof was underproofed, dough was tough to stretch. Good char on the baking steel but HEB whole milk mozz was too moist to shred.
notes: 1-day cold proof was underproofed — dough was hard to stretch, kept springing back
Used baking steel, preheated 1 hour at ~530°F (275°C), dropped to ~485°F (250°C) by the time pizza went in
HEB whole milk mozzarella was too moist to shred — had to tear by hand
8 min total bake on steel, rotated at 4 min mark, finished with 2 min under high broil
Good char on bottom from the steel, crust was crispy but slightly tough from underproofing

cook_log.summary: Second bake with a hydration mix-up during mise (weighed flour amount as water), producing the densest dough ever. Stretching improved after watching a tutorial, but crust burned from sugar at 550°F — may not need sugar for browning on steel.
notes: Hydration mixup during mise en place — weighed 288g flour (the water amount) instead of 463g. Dough was very watery. Added extra flour to compensate but the result was the densest pizza dough ever — gluten never developed properly from the two-stage flour addition
Bulk fermented overnight in the fridge. Pulled out next day, split into 2 balls, room temp proof ~5 hours total (4 hours + 1 hour during final oven preheat)
Poke test passed — dough balls sprang back after second ferment
Preheated oven to 550°F with pizza steel for ~2 hours. Steel clocked in at ~520°F at bake time
Dough stretched out much better than Try 1 — reviewed a YouTube stretching tutorial beforehand. Not afraid of it tearing this time, better size overall
Bake: 4 min on steel, rotated, 4 more min, then ~2 min under high broil
Crust was pretty burned — likely from the sugar in the dough. Oven at 550 + pizza steel may be hot enough to not need sugar for browning
Topping order: sauce → fresh grated Parmigiano-Reggiano (generous) → HEB low-moisture whole milk mozz (bagged) → pepperoni
HEB low-moisture mozz melted perfectly and didn't need shredding — much more convenient than Try 1's block mozz. Trade-off: less tangy flavor
Second pizza: ran out of pepperoni, did half pepperoni / half extra cheese. Cheesier side bubbled nicely
Sauce was jarred pizza sauce (not San Marzano) — want to get Sclafani next time
Forgot to measure dough ball yield
Bigger pizza size meant better pepperoni distribution compared to Try 1
Despite the char and dense crumb, good crunch and taste overall

Broiler is a separate drawer under the main oven — transferred pizza to a tray (not the steel) to avoid further bottom char. Two rack positions in the drawer; first pizza on upper rack (very close to flame), second pizza on lower rack. Broiler bubbled the cheese nicely. The crust burning was from the sugar, not the broiler

next_time.text: Consider lowering or removing sugar — oven at 550 + pizza steel provides enough heat for browning without it
Get Sclafani crushed tomatoes for proper sauce
Add Parmigiano-Reggiano as an ingredient in the recipe (sauce → parm → mozz → pepperoni layer order)

Try the 2-3 day cold proof (carried over — did overnight this time, still want to try longer)

cook_log.summary: Third bake — removed all sugar, 3-day cold proof, first time with TJ's mozz and homemade Sclafani sauce. Best pizza yet. No extra flour needed for shaping — dough handled like a dream.
notes: Removed all sugar from the dough (0g instead of recipe's 19g)
Rounded dough built nicely — patience paid off, let it sit before manipulating
No extra flour needed for rounding or shaping — stretched and worked dough into a ball completely flour-free
Dough was warm from washing machine running nearby — measured 77°F with laser thermometer (unsure of accuracy)
Dough volume in greased Cambro: ~1 quart at base, ~1.5 quart at peak
1 hour counter rest before overnight cold bulk ferment (into fridge ~12:30am)
Divided next day at ~12:24pm — total dough weight 765g, split nearly perfectly (~382g each). Portions back in fridge
Taken out ~11:45am on bake day (Feb 18) — effectively a 3-day process (mixed evening of Feb 16)
Pizza stone at 520°F at bake time, dough at 77°F after stretching
Used homemade NY pizza sauce (proofed Sclafani recipe) — much better than jarred. Wished I'd made it the night before to let flavors develop
Finally used Trader Joe's low-moisture mozz — better flavor, more depth than HEB
Toppings: sauce → fresh grated Parmigiano-Reggiano → TJ's mozz → Boar's Head pepperoni → fresh jalapeño slices (pre-bake)
1st pizza: 4 min on steel, rotate, 4 min, then broiler — broiler slightly too long at 1.5 min, aim for ~1 min. Crust less burned than last time, a little fractured and crunchy
2nd pizza: stone slightly cooler at 500°F. Dough ball sat out longer — incredibly malleable, almost scared it would rip but the dough held strong
Pepperoni shifted to one side when launching into oven — toppings not as evenly distributed after launch
Only light burn on crust this time — wonders if olive oil should also be removed for a leaner dough at these temps

ingredients.name: Low-Moisture Mozzarella
ingredients.note: Low-moisture, high-fat, whole milk mozzarella is mandatory — it shreds clean and melts right

states.title: Prepare Workspace
states.direction: Gather all vessels, equipment, and ingredients. Weigh out bread flour, water, yeast, olive oil, salt, and sugar into separate containers.
states.exit_condition: All ingredients weighed, vessels and equipment laid out

states.title: Mix Autolyse
states.direction: In the stand mixer bowl (V1), combine 463g bread flour, 288g water, and 6g instant yeast. Stir with the dough hook on speed 1 just until no dry flour remains.
states.exit_condition: Flour, water, and yeast combined into a shaggy mass with no dry flour visible

notes.text: Jacob Burton adds yeast to the autolyse water — he says it does not affect gluten formation

states.title: Autolyse Rest
states.direction: Cover the mixer bowl with plastic wrap and let the dough rest for 30 minutes at room temperature. Do not add salt, oil, or sugar yet.
states.exit_condition: 30 minutes elapsed, dough is more cohesive and slightly extensible

notes.text: The autolyse hydrates the flour and begins gluten development passively, reducing knead time

states.title: Add Enrichments
states.direction: Add 18g olive oil, 19g sugar, and 8g salt to the autolyse dough in the mixer bowl (V1).
states.exit_condition: Oil, sugar, and salt added on top of the dough, ready for kneading

notes.text: Olive oil adds extensibility and browning to the crust. Sugar promotes Maillard browning.

At 550°F with a preheated steel/stone, the 19g sugar may cause excessive browning. Consider reducing to 10g or omitting entirely if your oven runs hot — the Maillard reaction on the flour proteins provides sufficient browning at these temperatures.

states.title: Knead — First Pass
states.direction: Knead in the stand mixer (V1) on speed 2 for 4 minutes. The dough should begin to pull away from the sides of the bowl.
states.exit_condition: 4 minutes elapsed, dough is starting to come together and pull from the bowl sides

states.title: Knead — Second Pass
states.direction: Let the dough rest briefly in the bowl (1–2 minutes), then knead again on speed 2 for 4 more minutes. Total knead time is 8 minutes.
states.exit_condition: Dough is smooth, elastic, and pulls cleanly from the bowl sides

states.title: Window Pane Test
states.direction: Pinch off a small piece of dough and gently stretch it between your fingers. It should stretch thin enough to see light through without tearing.
states.exit_condition: Dough stretches thin enough to see light through without tearing

notes.text: If the dough tears before becoming translucent, knead for 1–2 more minutes and re-test

states.title: Round Dough
states.direction: Turn the dough out onto a clean surface. Using both hands, cup the dough and pull it toward you repeatedly to build surface tension. Tuck the edges underneath to form a taut ball.
states.exit_condition: Dough is shaped into a smooth, taut ball with good surface tension

states.title: Bulk Ferment
states.direction: Place the rounded dough into a lightly oiled large bowl (V2). Cover with plastic wrap and let ferment at room temperature for 2 hours.
states.exit_condition: Dough has roughly doubled in size, approximately 2 hours elapsed

notes.text: For more complex flavor, skip the room-temperature rise and cold ferment overnight in the fridge (8–16 hours). Remove 1 hour before dividing to take the chill off.

states.title: Divide Portions
states.direction: Turn the fermented dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Using a bench scraper, divide into 2 equal portions of approximately 388g each.
states.exit_condition: Dough divided into 2 portions of approximately 388g each

states.title: Round Portions
states.direction: Flatten each portion into a disc, then tuck the edges underneath to form a tight round ball. Place each ball on a parchment-lined sheet tray (V3) sprayed with non-stick spray. Spray the tops of the dough balls with non-stick spray, then cover loosely with plastic wrap.
states.exit_condition: Both portions rounded, placed on parchment-lined tray, sprayed, and covered with plastic wrap

notes.text: The non-stick spray on top prevents the plastic wrap from sticking and tearing the dough skin during proofing

states.title: Proof Portions
states.direction: Let the dough balls proof at room temperature for 1 to 1.5 hours. They should puff up and feel light and airy.
states.exit_condition: Dough balls are puffy and visibly expanded, spring back slowly when gently poked

notes.text: For even more flavor development, proof in the refrigerator for 12–24 hours instead. Remove 30–60 minutes before stretching to take the chill off.
Begin preheating the oven and pizza stone at least 45 minutes before you plan to bake

states.title: Preheat Pizza Stone
states.direction: Place the pizza stone (V4) on the middle oven rack. Preheat the oven to 550°F (288°C). Allow at least 45 minutes for the stone to fully saturate with heat.
states.exit_condition: Oven at 550°F (288°C) and stone fully preheated for at least 45 minutes

notes.text: A fully preheated stone is essential — it provides the intense bottom heat that creates a properly charred NY-style crust

states.title: Stretch Dough
states.direction: Sprinkle the wooden pizza peel (V5) with 7g cornmeal. Place one dough ball on a lightly floured surface. Using your fingertips, press from the center outward, pushing air toward the edges to form the crust rim. Pick up the dough and drape it over your knuckles, gently stretching and rotating until you have a 30–33cm (12–13 inch) disc. Never use a rolling pin. Transfer to the cornmeal-dusted peel.
states.exit_condition: Dough stretched to a 30–33cm disc with puffy edge crust, resting on cornmeal-dusted peel

notes.text: Never roll pizza dough — rolling pops the gas bubbles that create the airy, puffy crust
Give the peel a shake before topping to make sure the dough slides freely on the cornmeal

states.title: Top Pizza
states.direction: Spread 88g raw San Marzano tomato sauce over the dough, leaving a 2cm border for the crust. Add any non-cheese toppings. Top with 175g low-moisture mozzarella, torn or shredded. Place 88g pepperoni on top of the cheese so it browns and crisps directly.
states.exit_condition: Pizza topped with sauce, cheese, and pepperoni (pepperoni on top of cheese)

notes.text: Pepperoni goes on top of the cheese — this is intentional so it browns, crisps, and cups up during baking
Layering sauce → grated Parmigiano-Reggiano → mozzarella → pepperoni adds a savory base layer under the mozz. The parm melts into the sauce and creates a flavor bridge between the two.
Do not overload with sauce or the center will be soggy and the pizza will not slide off the peel

states.title: Bake Pizza
states.direction: Open the oven and slide the pizza from the peel onto the preheated stone (V4) with a quick forward-and-back motion. Bake at 550°F (288°C) for 8–12 minutes. Repeat the stretch, top, and bake process for the second pizza.
states.exit_condition: Cheese is bubbly and lightly browned, crust is puffed and golden with charred spots

notes.text: Check at 8 minutes — ovens vary. Rotate the pizza halfway through if your oven has hot spots.

states.title: Cool & Slice
states.direction: Use the peel to slide the baked pizza onto a wire rack or cutting board. Let it rest for 2–3 minutes. Cut into 8 slices. Serve immediately.
states.exit_condition: Pizza rested, cut into 8 slices, ready to serve

notes.text: A brief rest lets the cheese set slightly so it does not slide off when you pick up a slice

methods.detail: Heat a dry pan over medium-high heat. Add 1–3 slices of cold pizza and heat for about 2 minutes until the bottom starts to crisp. Add 1–1.5 tsp water and immediately cover the pan. Steam covered for 30 seconds. Uncover, let any remaining water boil off, and continue cooking until the bottom is firm and crispy, about 1 minute. Don't burn the crust. Results taste exactly like fresh — crispy bottom, melty cheese, soft top.
350–400°F for about 5 minutes. Quick and effective, crisps the bottom well.
